note: Each stage names a fixture, a regular expression, and how many lines of
the page's rendered text must match it. Deliberately an assertion about
the DOM after script has run rather than about the framework: a row reads
'item 0' and appears in the served HTML nowhere, so the count is a claim
that a component tree was built and committed, and it stays true if React
Text rather than a CSS selector because `open --json` has no selector
engine on the far side. An earlier draft said 'selector' and matched text
anyway, which is a harness lying about what it checks.
There are no timing bounds here on purpose. Timing is reported and never
gated: a latency gate in CI is a flake factory, and ROADMAP B15.12a's

stages.name: react
stages.why: React 18 createRoot render. The <li>s are not in the served HTML.

stages.name: vue
stages.why: Vue 3 createApp/mount, including its runtime template compiler.

stages.name: ssr-hydrate
stages.why: The served markup has one row; twelve means hydration ran. An engine that hydrates nothing still renders something correct here, which is why the count is the assertion.

stages.name: spa-router
stages.why: fetch of a same-origin JSON resource, then a render. Composite with pushState.

stages.name: spa-route-state
stages.why: history.pushState actually moved location.hash, rather than the render merely happening.

stages.name: modern-js
stages.why: The language and platform constructs a current bundle assumes. A gap here kills a page on line one.

stages.name: timers
stages.why: Timer and microtask ordering through the settle. On a virtual clock this costs no wall time, which the reported latency should show.

stages.name: import-map
stages.why: ROADMAP B19.8: a bare specifier resolves because the page declared where it goes, not because the engine invented a CDN.
